purpose: One bounded semantic judgment per source for each UTEX 2973 CDS locus: which of the lab's eleven broad function categories a computational annotation source places the protein in. The GO IEA source is judged from the locus's IEA Gene Ontology terms alone; the PCC 7942 source is judged from the joined PCC 7942 RefSeq product name alone. Neither judgment ever becomes a reviewed assignment.
blinding: Request states never contain a locus tag, gene symbol, the UTEX 2973 product, the lab-reviewed category, the other source's annotation, or any essentiality status. The GO request holds only GO terms; the PCC request holds only the PCC 7942 product text, so each source's category is independent of the other and of the reviewed table it is later compared with.

evidence_policy: Judge only the text in the state. Do not guess which gene this is and do not use knowledge about a particular gene beyond what the text states.
Choose the single category whose definition best matches the specific function the text states. When the text names one specific activity, process, or complex, choose the category that lists it.

Choose unknown-or-unclassified when the text is a hypothetical protein, a domain, family, repeat, or DUF name with no stated function, or only generic terms such as binding a common ligand, a broad enzyme class without a named substrate or process, or a location such as membrane or cytoplasm.
Choose other-characterized only when the text states a specific function that none of the nine specific categories lists.
These are automated annotations, so answer about the role the text states, not about whether the protein is important.

instructions.task: Using only the Gene Ontology terms in `go_annotations`, choose the one broad function category that best describes this protein from a photosynthetic cyanobacterium.
instructions.term_policy: A term counts only when it names a specific process, activity, or complex. Binding a common ligand, ion, ATP, DNA, or protein, belonging to a broad enzyme class, or being located in a membrane, the cytoplasm, or the thylakoid is not specific on its own; such terms never decide the category and, when they are the only terms, the answer is unknown-or-unclassified.

instructions.task: Using only the RefSeq product name in `pcc_7942_refseq_product`, choose the one broad function category that best describes this protein from a photosynthetic cyanobacterium.
instructions.name_policy: A product name counts only when it names a specific enzyme, complex subunit, transporter, regulator, or process. A name that is only a family, domain, repeat, DUF, or hypothetical designation states no function and the answer is unknown-or-unclassified.

photosynthetic-light-reactions.label: Photosynthetic light reactions
photosynthetic-light-reactions.definition: Light capture and photosynthetic electron transport.
includes: photosystem I or photosystem II subunits, reaction-center proteins, and their assembly, stabilizing, or repair factors
phycobilisome proteins: phycocyanin, allophycocyanin, phycoerythrin, linker polypeptides, and phycobiliprotein lyases
cytochrome b6f complex, plastocyanin, cytochrome c6, photosynthetic ferredoxin, ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase
photosynthetic electron transport, light harvesting, and photosystem-bound photoprotection

carbon-and-nutrient-metabolism.label: Carbon and nutrient metabolism
carbon-and-nutrient-metabolism.definition: Carbon fixation, central and intermediary metabolism, and nutrient assimilation.
includes: RuBisCO and its activase, carboxysome shell and carbonic anhydrase, Calvin cycle, carbon fixation, inorganic carbon concentration
glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, pentose phosphate pathway, TCA cycle enzymes, glycogen and carbohydrate metabolism
nitrogen, sulfur, and phosphorus assimilation: nitrate and nitrite reductases, glutamine synthetase, sulfate reduction, polyphosphate
amino acid, nucleotide, fatty acid, and lipid biosynthesis or degradation

atp-production-and-respiration.label: ATP production and respiration
atp-production-and-respiration.definition: ATP synthase and respiratory electron transport.
includes: F0F1 ATP synthase subunits
respiratory chain: NAD(P)H dehydrogenase (NDH-1 and NDH-2) subunits, succinate dehydrogenase, cytochrome c oxidase, quinol and alternative terminal oxidases, aerobic respiration
hydrogenases and their maturation

pigment-and-cofactor-biosynthesis.label: Pigment and cofactor biosynthesis
pigment-and-cofactor-biosynthesis.definition: Synthesis, salvage, or modification of pigments, cofactors, and vitamins.
includes: chlorophyll, carotenoid, phycobilin, heme, porphyrin, and tetrapyrrole biosynthesis, magnesium chelatase, ferrochelatase
cofactor and vitamin biosynthesis or modification: NAD and NAD+ kinase, riboflavin/FAD, coenzyme A, folate, thiamine, cobalamin, biotin, lipoate, quinones, molybdopterin, pyridoxal phosphate
iron-sulfur cluster assembly

translation-and-protein-maintenance.label: Translation and protein maintenance
includes: ribosomal proteins, ribosome structure, translation initiation, elongation, and termination factors
aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (tRNA ligases) and tRNA aminoacylation
general chaperones and folding factors: DnaK, DnaJ, GroEL/GroES, HslO, trigger factor, peptidyl-prolyl isomerases
protein quality control: Clp, Lon, FtsH, and other proteases, protein degradation

dna-and-rna-processing.label: DNA and RNA processing
dna-and-rna-processing.definition: Replication, transcription machinery, and nucleic-acid processing.
includes: DNA replication: DNA polymerases, primase, helicases, ligases, single-stranded DNA-binding protein, topoisomerases and gyrase, chromosome partitioning
core RNA polymerase subunits, transcription elongation, termination, and antitermination factors
RNA processing, degradation, and modification: ribonucleases, rRNA and tRNA maturation and modification, RNA helicases
DNA restriction, methylation, and modification

transport-and-envelope.label: Transport and envelope
transport-and-envelope.definition: Membrane transport, protein secretion, and cell-envelope synthesis.
includes: transporters, channels, porins, ABC systems, antiporters, symporters, efflux pumps, and their substrate-binding, permease, or ATP-binding subunits
protein translocation and secretion: Sec, Tat, SRP, YidC, type II/IV secretion systems, lipoproteins
cell wall and outer membrane synthesis: peptidoglycan, penicillin-binding proteins, lipopolysaccharide and lipid A, lipid A export, capsule and exopolysaccharide
pili and flagella assembly

signaling-and-circadian-regulation.label: Signaling and circadian regulation
signaling-and-circadian-regulation.definition: Sensing, signal transduction, and transcriptional or circadian regulation.
includes: two-component sensor histidine kinases and response regulators, phosphorelay
DNA-binding transcriptional regulators and transcription factors, RNA polymerase sigma factors
serine/threonine protein kinases and phosphatases, second-messenger synthesis or hydrolysis (cAMP, c-di-GMP, c-di-AMP), GGDEF and EAL proteins
circadian clock proteins KaiA, KaiB, KaiC, LdpA, CikA, SasA, RpaA, light sensing, chemotaxis

stress-and-repair.label: Stress and repair
stress-and-repair.definition: Defence against and recovery from damage or stress.
includes: oxidative stress defence: peroxiredoxin, catalase, superoxide dismutase, thioredoxin, glutaredoxin, oxidant detoxification
DNA repair and recombination for repair: RecA, UvrABC, MutS/MutL, photolyase, SOS response

heat, cold, osmotic, light, and metal stress proteins whose name states a stress role: Hsp20/alpha-crystallin, cold-shock protein, universal stress protein, compatible-solute synthesis, orange carotenoid protein
metal sequestration and detoxification

other-characterized.label: Other characterized
other-characterized.definition: A specific, stated function that fits none of the nine categories above.
includes: cell division and cell shape: FtsZ, FtsQ, Min proteins, septum formation, cytokinesis
mobile genetic elements and phage: transposase, integrase, phage proteins, DNA integration
toxin-antitoxin systems, natural competence, twitching motility
secondary metabolism and any other named function outside the nine categories

unknown-or-unclassified.label: Unknown or unclassified
includes: hypothetical protein
a domain, family, repeat, or DUF name with no stated function (for example FHA domain-containing protein, HEAT repeat protein, DUF3598 family protein)
only generic terms: binding a common ligand, ion, ATP, DNA, or protein; catalytic activity, transferase or hydrolase without a named substrate; membrane or cytoplasm location
